html:
Bunyoro, or Bunyoro-Kitara, is a kingdom of western Uganda, east of Lake Albert, and was one of the most powerful states of the Great Lakes region from the 1500s to the 1800s. The map shows it from 1815 to 1900.

Its kings, the Omukama, come from the Babito dynasty, which tradition says took over from the legendary Kitara of the Bachwezi. Bunyoro drew its wealth from iron, salt from Lake Albert and cattle.

In the 1700s and 1800s Buganda took more and more of its land. Omukama Kabalega, who ruled from 1870, rebuilt the army with guns bought from traders from the north and fought both Buganda and the British for years. In 1899 he was captured and exiled, and Britain gave large parts of Bunyoro to Buganda, the "lost counties", which were returned only after a vote in 1964. The kingdom was abolished in 1967 and restored as a cultural monarchy in 1993.
